0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part I ) was adopted by the Indian Standards

Institution on 24 September 1980, after the draft finalized by the Capacitors Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council.

0.2 The object of this Indian Standard ( Part I ) is to establish uniform requirements for judging the mechanical, electrical and climatic properties of fixed polyester film dielectric and similar dielectric direct current capacitors, for rated voltage not exceeding 6 300 V, and using electrodes of thin meta foils, intended to be used in electronic and telecommunication equipment. 0.3 This standard requires reference to IS : 7305 ( Part I) -1973* in which details of various tests prescribed have been fully covered. Only the appropriate degrees of severity and any other special conditions relating to certain tests have been included in this standard. 0.4 This standard does not cover capacitors for radio suppression which are covered by IS : 3723 ( Part I )-19787. 0.5 While preparing this standard, following: interference from the

assistance has been derived

a) IEC Document 40 ( Central Office ) 417 : Draft Sectional Specification for Fixed Polyethylene-terephthalate Film Dielectric Metal Foil Capacitors for Direct Current; Selection of Methods The International Electroof Tests and General Requirements. technical Commission ( IEC ).
*Fixed capacitors used in electronic equipment: tests. tcapacitors for radio interference suppression methods of tests (jirsf w&ion ). Part I General requirements and

: Part I General requirements and

3

IS. : 9638

( Part I ) - 1980 Specification The Ministry for Capacitors, Fixed, of Defence, India.

b) JSS : 50212 ( 1972 ) : Detail Paper/Polyester Dielectric.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard relates to fixed polyester film dielectric and similar dielectric direct current capacitors, for rated voltages not exceeding 6 300 V, and using electrodes of thin metal foils intended for use in electronic equipment. For capacitors with rated voltages exceeding 1 000 V, additional tests and requirements may be specified in the detail specification. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 In addition to the terms and definitions 1973*, the following definitick shall apply. specified in IS : 7305 ( Part I)-

2.2 Rated Voltage UR - The rated voltage is the maximum dc voltage which may be applied continuously to the terminals of a capacitor at the rated temperature.
NATE 1 -The sum the voltage and the peak ac voltage to bc applied to the capacitor shall not exceed the rated voltage. NOTE 2 -The value of the peak ac voltage shall not exceed percentages of the rated voltage at the frequencies stated and shall 280 v: 50 Hz 100 Hz 1000 Hz 10 000 Hz unless otherwise 3. 20 percent 15 percent 3 percent 1 percent the following be maximum

specified in the detail specification.

YI : 8.3.2.1 The capacitance shall be measured at a frequency of 1 000 For capacitors whose values are greater than 1 Mfd and rated Hz. voltage up to 3 kV the measuring frequency should be 50 Hz or 100 Hz. But for capacitors whose values are less than 1 Mfd and rated voltage of 3 kV or more, the measuring frequency shall be 1 kHz. The applied peak voltage at 1 000 Hz shall not exceed 3 percent of the rated voltage and the applied peak voltage at 50 to 100 Hz shall not exceed 15 percent of the rated voltage with a maximum of 100 V ( 70 V rms ). 8.3.2.2 The capacitance shall be within the specified tolerance.

8.3.4 Insulation Resistance - This test shal1 be carried out in accordance with 7.3.6 of IS : 7305 (Part I )-1973* with the following details. 8.3.4.1 Before the measurement, the capacitor shall be fully discharged. 8.3.7 Dielectric Absorption - Unless otherwise specified, the capacitor shall be charge at the dc voltage rating for 1 hour f 1 minute, The initial surge current shall not exceed 50 mA. At the end of this period, the capacitor shall be disconnected from the power source and discharged through a 5 ohm f 5 percent resistor for 10 f 1 seconds. The discharged resistor shall be disconnected from the capacitor at the end of the lo-second discharge period, and the voltage remaining on the capacitor ( recovery voltage ) shall be measured with an electrometer or other suitable device having an input resistance of 10 000 MS1 or greater. Recovery voltage shall be read at the maximum voltage within a 15 minutes period. The dielectric absorption shall be computed from the following formula :
